sections.html:
Franklin sits along the Harpeth River roughly 21 miles south of Nashville, and Williamson County runs its government from here. July 2025 put the population at 90,226, a gain of 8.0 percent on the 83,454 residents of 2020. Only six Tennessee cities are larger.

Housing here is expensive. Owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $705,400 for 2020 to 2024, over twice the national median of $332,700. Among 33,998 households, 63.8 percent are owners. A homeowner with a mortgage spends a median $2,542 monthly, one without a loan spends $712, and renters pay $1,923. Median household income is $119,528.

Expect buyers who weigh a big purchase carefully, so organized paperwork and a clean title help. Interstate 65 touches the east edge of town, and the Mack Hatcher bypass loops around the business district. Five historic districts hold National Register listings, and older neighborhoods fall under local protection rules. Own a house near the square? Phone City Hall before you plan any exterior repair work.

Inside city limits the levy is $0.296 on every $100 of assessed value, and the 2026-27 budget proposal holds it steady. That figure splits into a $0.2310 base rate for operations and debt and $0.0650 that came in after the latest reappraisal to pay for infrastructure and city services. City staff describe it as among the lowest in the state. Values are reset by the county assessor on a four-year cycle.

You will see only one statement. The Williamson County Trustee collects county, Franklin Special School District and city taxes on a single bill. For the amount on a particular parcel, ring the trustee at 615-790-5709. Questions about assessed value or a billing address belong with the assessor at 615-790-5708.

The trustee has no power to waive, prorate or release tax or interest. The owner on January 1 is the one on record for that year's bill, which means a mid-year seller hands the bill to the buyer through the closing statement.

The bill follows the same schedule every year, and a payment made before March carries no interest.

Williamson County tax bill calendar
DateWhat happens
Early OctoberStatements go out by mail
First Monday of OctoberPayment window opens
End of FebruaryFinal day to pay with no interest
March 1Interest of 1.5 percent begins and is added again on the first of each following month

Selling in autumn? The buyer's title company will ask whether this year's bill is settled or still open. Dig out your statement early. If none arrived, say so up front so the closing agent can look the parcel up.

sections.h2: School zones, utilities and monthly fees
sections.html:
Franklin Special School District teaches kindergarten through eighth grade across most of the city, and Williamson County Schools take over for high school. A few outlying areas sit in the county district for all grades. Many families start by checking the school boundary, so know which district covers your address. Private choices nearby include Battle Ground Academy, Franklin Classical School, Franklin Christian Academy, Montessori School of Franklin, New Hope Academy and Thales Academy.

Monthly costs are the next question. The city plans to lift residential trash and recycling by $1, to $34 a month, in fiscal 2027, and stormwater charges are projected to add about $20.70 a year to most bills. Water and sewer rates went up 6 percent and 5.7 percent on January 1, 2026.

Most residents get water from the city. Pockets are served by the Mallory Valley, Milcrofton and HB&TS utility districts. Middle Tennessee Electric supplies TVA power and Atmos Energy supplies gas. Confirm the providers for your street before a buyer wonders.

The Williamson County Register of Deeds handles Franklin deeds from 1320 West Main Street, Suite 201, open weekdays from 8 to 4:30. A fee calculator and electronic filing are available, and the phone line is 615-790-5706.

State taxes ride along with recording. Realty transfer tax is 37 cents per $100 of price. Mortgage tax is 11.5 cents per $100 on a buyer's loan beyond its first $2,000. The register gathers both amounts and forwards them to the state.

sections.h2: What happens after you accept an offer
sections.html:
Once a contract is signed, a title company takes over the paperwork. It checks who holds title, learns the balance on your mortgage, hunts for liens or unpaid bills and drafts the deed. Under Tennessee practice the buyer, as grantee, owes the transfer tax, while the sales contract settles every other split.

  • Before saying yes, locate your latest tax statement and your lender's contact details.
  • Ask the title company for three answers ahead of closing: the loan payoff, any tax balance and the plan for recording.
  • Remember the trustee refuses to prorate, so the January 1 owner rule drives how the bill is divided.
  • Sign the deed; the title company then walks it to the register.

Cash changes the calendar. No bank means no loan approval and no lender appraisal, and those two steps are where financed deals most often stall. Clear title is still required, so everything in the list above applies to a cash purchase too.

If the house needs work, a cash offer folds the repairs into its price. You skip staging, open houses and the repair list that arrives after a buyer's inspection. Judge offers by what lands in your pocket after repairs and carrying costs, not by the number on the first page.

Pull together the paperwork from your own purchase, the newest tax statement and any permit records for work you paid for. Own in a historic district? Add the approvals City Hall issued for earlier exterior changes, since a buyer's agent may ask.

Then pick a route. An agent listing reaches the most buyers, which counts in a high-priced market. Handling it yourself saves the commission but puts the contract and scheduling on your plate. A cash sale gives up some price in return for speed and a closing date you can count on. Whichever you pick, deeds go to the same register and tax bills come from the same trustee.

A Franklin tax balance does not disappear when the house sells. Interest starts on March 1 and repeats each month, so an old debt swells without announcement. Behind on the bill? Call the trustee for an exact payoff figure before you set a closing date, then have the title company pay it out of your proceeds at the table. Nobody at the trustee's office can reduce the charge, so an early number spares you a nasty surprise on the settlement statement.

A cash buyer can close fast even with a balance outstanding, because the payoff is subtracted from the price. Mention the debt on the first call with any buyer.

faqs.q: How many people live in Franklin?
faqs.a: About 90,226 as of July 2025, up from 83,454 in 2020. Only six Tennessee cities are bigger.

faqs.q: What is Franklin's city property tax rate?
faqs.a: The levy is $0.296 per $100 of assessed value, and the 2026-27 budget proposal leaves it alone. County and school district charges arrive on the same bill.

faqs.q: When are Williamson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment opens the first Monday of October and stays open until the end of February. From March 1, interest of 1.5 percent applies and repeats monthly.

faqs.q: Who pays Tennessee's transfer tax on a Franklin sale?
faqs.a: The buyer pays it, as grantee on the deed. The rate is 37 cents per $100 of price, and the register collects it at filing.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a Franklin house?
faqs.a: Williamson County Register of Deeds, Suite 201 at 1320 West Main Street. Call 615-790-5706 with fee questions.
